mainTopic: The soldiers' גט in דוד's wars, and whether a husband is believed with a claim of פתח פתוח, to forbid his wife or to take away her כתובה
overview: This amud opens with the rule that every soldier in the wars of בית דוד wrote his wife a גט כריתות before leaving. The source is the פסוק 'ואת ערבתם תקח,' which רב יוסף reads as the marriage bond. The גמרא then turns to a husband's claim of פתח פתוח, that he found his bride was not a virgin. אביי tries to prove from the rule that a בתולה marries on Wednesday that this claim is believed to forbid her to him, as רבי אלעזר holds. The proof is rejected, because the משנה may be talking about a claim of 'no blood.' Next, רב יהודה quotes שמואל: a husband who claims פתח פתוח is believed to make his wife lose her כתובה. רב יוסף asks why שמואל needs to say this, since the משנה about a groom eating at his father-in-law's house in יהודה seems to teach it already. That proof is rejected the same way: the משנה may be about a claim of 'no blood,' so שמואל's ruling teaches something new.

steps.title: Soldiers in דוד's wars gave their wives a divorce
steps.stepSummary: Anyone who went out to fight in the wars of בית דוד wrote a גט כריתות for his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone who goes out to a war of בית דוד writes a גט for his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: every soldier in דוד's army gave his wife a גט before going to war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of this גט, if a soldier did not come back, his wife was already divorced and could remarry. This rule explains how בת שבע was not a married woman when דוד took her, since אוריה had gone out to war.

keyTerms.meaning: A bill of divorce that fully cuts off the marriage
A war fought by the royal house of דוד

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule answers how בת שבע was permitted to דוד: she was already divorced from אוריה.

phrases.english: Anyone who goes out to a war of the house of David
writes a bill of divorce for his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the section with a rule that answers the earlier question about בת שבע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every soldier in דוד's wars gave his wife a גט כריתות before leaving.

steps.title: The פסוק behind the soldiers' divorce
steps.stepSummary: The rule is drawn from the פסוק 'and take their pledge,' which רב יוסף explains as the marriage bond between husband and wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And greet your brothers in peace, and take their pledge.' What does 'take their pledge' mean? רב יוסף taught: the things that are shared between him and her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק as the source for the soldiers' גט, and רב יוסף explains the hard word in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישי told דוד to bring back the 'ערבתם' of his brothers at the front. רב יוסף reads ערבתם like מעורבין, 'shared things,' meaning the marriage between husband and wife. So taking their ערבה means taking the גט that ends the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: Their pledge, read here as 'what is shared between them'
He taught (a teaching from a ברייתא)
Things that are mixed together or shared

steps.whatToRemember: Soldiers in דוד's wars gave a גט before battle. The source is 'ואת ערבתם תקח,' read as the shared marriage bond.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And greet your brothers in peace,'
'and take their pledge.'
What is 'and take their pledge'?
Rav Yosef taught:
Matters that are shared between him and her.
phrases.notes: There's a wordplay here: ערבתם sounds like מעורבין, so the 'pledge' is the marriage bond that the גט ends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the rule in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that soldiers of בית דוד gave their wives a גט
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 17:18, 'ואת ערבתם תקח,' as explained by רב יוסף

steps.title: אביי brings a משנה to support רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה that a בתולה marries on Wednesday supports רבי אלעזר. The reason she doesn't marry on Thursday is so the husband's anger doesn't cool before he can go to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We too have learned this. A virgin is married on Wednesday. On Wednesday, yes; on Thursday, no. What is the reason? Because his mind would cool down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes topic. אביי begins building a proof from a משנה for רבי אלעזר, who said a husband is believed when he claims he found his bride was not a virgin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courts sat on Mondays and Thursdays. A Wednesday wedding lets the husband go to court the very next morning with any complaint. A Thursday wedding would make him wait until Monday, and by then he might calm down and drop his claim. This is only the setup; the next steps show what the claim is for.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (a source supporting a view)
A virgin bride
The fourth day of the week, Wednesday
His mind cooling off, his anger calming down

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not just teaching when to make a wedding. He is using that rule as the first part of a proof about the husband's claim, which finishes in step 6.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
We too have learned it:
phrases.notes: 'It' means רבי אלעזר's view: a husband is believed when he claims he found an 'open opening.'

phrases.english: A virgin is married on the fourth day.
On the fourth day, yes;
on the fifth day, no.
What is the reason?
Because his mind would cool down.
phrases.notes: After a Thursday wedding he'd have to wait until Monday for court, and he might calm down and not complain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: a proof for רבי אלעזר's view on the claim of פתח פתוח.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's view that a husband is believed with the claim of פתח פתוח
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that a בתולה is married on Wednesday, so the husband's anger won't cool before court

steps.title: What does his claim accomplish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the husband's claim is for. If it were only about the כתובה, he could simply choose to pay it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what purpose? If it is about giving her the כתובה, let him give it to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask why it matters if the husband's anger cools. It rules out money as the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only issue were losing out on the כתובה money, there would be no need to worry. A husband is allowed to pay more than he must. So the concern must be about something more serious.

keyTerms.meaning: And for what purpose?
The marriage contract and the payment it promises the wife

phrases.english: And for what purpose?
If it is about giving her the marriage contract,
let him give it to her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what is at stake in the worry from step 3, and rules out the כתובה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the husband's claim accomplishes that makes us worry about his anger cooling

steps.title: The claim is to forbid her to him
steps.stepSummary: The concern is not money. His claim could make her forbidden to him, so we want him to bring the claim to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is to forbid her to him, in a case where he makes a claim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the claim matters because it can make the wife forbidden to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she was not a virgin, she may have been with another man after the אירוסין, which would make her forbidden to her husband. That is an איסור, not just money, so we don't want him to let it go. This sets up the question of which kind of claim the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: To make her forbidden to him
A claim brought before the court

phrases.english: Rather, it is to forbid her to him,
in a case where he makes a claim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4: the claim matters for איסור, not for money.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The worry is that he won't bring a claim that would make her forbidden to him.

steps.title: אביי's conclusion: the claim must be פתח פתוח
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests the claim in the משנה is פתח פתוח, which would prove that a husband is believed with that claim, as רבי אלעזר says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not talking about a case where he claims 'I found an open opening'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of אביי's proof. He says the claim the משנה worries about must be פתח פתוח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה cares about the husband reaching court with a claim of פתח פתוח, then that claim must be believed enough to forbid her. That is exactly רבי אלעזר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not? (a way of pushing a proof)
'An open opening': the husband's claim that he found she was not a virgin

phrases.english: What, is it not
where he makes the claim of 'an open opening'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו, דְּקָטָעֵין טַעֲנַת פֶּתַח פָּתוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof that began in step 3, using the answer from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר: a husband is believed with the claim of פתח פתוח
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's worry that the husband might not bring his claim to court

steps.title: No, the claim could be about blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה might mean a claim that there was no blood, not פתח פתוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is a case where he claims there was no blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down אביי's proof by reading the משנה another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A claim of 'no blood' can be checked and is easy to believe. A claim of פתח פתוח depends only on his own feeling. Since the משנה can be explained with the blood claim, it proves nothing about believing a claim of פתח פתוח.

keyTerms.meaning: The claim that there was no blood, as there would be with a virgin

steps.whatToRemember: אביי tried to prove רבי אלעזר's view from the Wednesday wedding rule. The proof is rejected because the משנה may be talking about a claim of 'no blood,' not פתח פתוח.

phrases.english: No,
it is where he makes a claim about blood.
phrases.notes: He means he found no blood, which would be there if she were a virgin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 6 by offering another case for the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not say רבי אלעזר is wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be explained as a claim of 'no blood,' so it does not have to be about פתח פתוח.

steps.title: שמואל: A husband claiming an open opening is believed about the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: a husband who says 'I found an open opening' is believed, so his wife loses her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A husband who says 'I found an open opening' is believed, and his wife loses her marriage contract.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל. A husband who claims פתח פתוח is believed, and that is enough to take away his wife's כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, אביי tried to prove רבי אלעזר's view that a פתח פתוח claim is believed to make her forbidden to him, and the proof was rejected. Here שמואל rules on a different result of the same claim: money. The husband is believed, and she loses her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'open opening': the husband's claim that he found his bride was not a virgin, without mentioning blood
Believed (his word is accepted)
To make her lose her כתובה (the marriage-contract money)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
One who says, "I found an open opening,"
is believed to make her lose her marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the claim of פתח פתוח from steps 3–7, but shifts from forbidding the wife to the money question: שמואל rules that the claim takes away her כתובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband claiming פתח פתוח is believed to make his wife lose her כתובה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Why do we need this? A משנה already teaches it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks what שמואל adds, quoting a משנה about a groom who eats at his father-in-law's house in יהודה without witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is שמואל teaching us? We already learned in a משנה: One who eats at his father-in-law's house in יהודה, without witnesses, cannot make a virginity claim, because we assume he was alone with her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges שמואל: why say this at all, if a משנה already seems to teach it? He quotes that משנה to set up his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יהודה, engaged couples were often alone together before the wedding. So a groom who ate there with no witnesses watching cannot later complain that his bride was not a virgin, since he may have been the one with her. רב יוסף is about to show that this משנה hides שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (what is new here?)
We already learned it (in a משנה)
His father-in-law
A virginity claim (claiming the bride was not a virgin)
Is alone with (her) in private

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן?
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: What is he teaching us?

phrases.aramaic: תְּנֵינָא: הָאוֹכֵל אֵצֶל חָמִיו בִּיהוּדָה שֶׁלֹּא בְּעֵדִים —
phrases.english: We already learned: One who eats at his father-in-law's house in Judea without witnesses —
phrases.notes: This is during the engagement, before the wedding. 'Without witnesses' means nobody was there to see that he was never alone with her.

phrases.english: cannot make a virginity claim,
because he is alone with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling as unnecessary because a משנה already seems to say it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a משנה already teaches that a husband is believed with a פתח פתוח claim, שמואל's statement adds nothing new.

steps.title: Reading the משנה: in the גליל he can make the claim
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's words 'in יהודה', רב יוסף reasons that in the גליל the groom can make the claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is in יהודה that he cannot make the claim; but in the גליל, he can make the claim.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף draws an inference from the משנה. Since it says 'in יהודה' he cannot claim, then in the גליל, where couples were not alone before the wedding, he can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the core of the proof. We now know there is a case where a virginity claim works. The next steps ask what that claim is for, and what the claim is.

keyTerms.meaning: But (here it means 'by contrast, in the other case')
The גליל, the northern region of ארץ ישראל, with a different custom from יהודה
He is able to make the claim

phrases.english: It is in Judea that he cannot make the claim,
but in the Galilee he can make the claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּיהוּדָה הוּא דְּלָא מָצֵי טָעֵין, הָא בַּגָּלִיל מָצֵי טָעֵין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה quoted in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband's virginity claim works in some case (the גליל)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה limiting the rule to יהודה

steps.title: What is the claim for? It cannot be about forbidding her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the claim in the גליל achieves. If it were about forbidding her to him, then why can't he do that in יהודה too?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what purpose is the claim? If it is to make her forbidden to him, then in יהודה, why not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the claim in the משנה is meant to do. It shows that it cannot be about making her forbidden to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being forbidden is about what the husband himself knows. If he knows he was never with her, a court's suspicion that he was alone with her should not stop his claim from forbidding her to him. Since the משנה says the claim fails in יהודה, the claim must be about something where the court's suspicion matters: money.

keyTerms.meaning: To make her forbidden to him (as a wife)
Why?

phrases.english: And for what? If it is to make her forbidden to him,
then in Judea, why not?
phrases.notes: He knows himself whether he was with her. So if his claim could forbid her, it should work in יהודה too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאי, אִי לְאוֹסְרָהּ עָלָיו, בִּיהוּדָה אַמַּאי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the claim from step 10 is meant to do, ruling out the option of forbidding her.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the virginity claim in the גליל achieves: forbidding her, or taking away her כתובה?

steps.title: So it is about the כתובה, and the claim must be פתח פתוח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes the claim is about making her lose her כתובה, and suggests the claim is פתח פתוח, which would match שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it to make her lose her marriage contract, where he makes a claim? And what claim? Isn't it the claim 'I found an open opening'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the claim must be about taking away her כתובה. It then suggests the claim is פתח פתוח, which would mean the משנה already teaches שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes רב יוסף's challenge. If the משנה is about money and the claim is פתח פתוח, then the משנה already says that a husband is believed with that claim to take away the כתובה. Then שמואל's statement would add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...? (introduces the only remaining option)
Isn't it...? (suggests the reading that proves the point)

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it to make her lose her marriage contract,
where he makes a claim?

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, דְּקָא טָעֵין טַעֲנַת ״פֶּתַח פָּתוּחַ״!
phrases.english: Isn't it where he makes the claim of "an open opening"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 and completes רב יוסף's proof that the משנה already teaches שמואל's rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The claim is to take away her כתובה, and it is a פתח פתוח claim, so the משנה already teaches שמואל's rule.

steps.title: No: the משנה may be about a claim of no blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה may mean a claim that there was no blood, not פתח פתוח. So שמואל's ruling teaches something new.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is where he makes a claim about blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב יוסף's reading. The משנה may be talking about a husband who claims he found no blood, so it does not teach anything about פתח פתוח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A claim of 'no blood' is a different kind of claim than פתח פתוח. Since the משנה can be read as being about blood, it does not prove that a husband is believed with פתח פתוח. So שמואל's ruling is needed to teach that.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejects the suggested reading)
A claim about blood (that he found no blood)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף tried to show that the משנה about eating at the father-in-law's house in יהודה already teaches שמואל's rule. It fails, because that משנה may be about a claim of no blood. So שמואל's rule, that a husband is believed with פתח פתוח to take away the כתובה, is a new teaching.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same rejection as step 7, but against a different proof. Each time, the answer is that the claim may be 'no blood' rather than פתח פתוח.

phrases.english: No, it is where he makes a claim about blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading in step 12, which answers רב יוסף's challenge in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the identification of the claim as פתח פתוח; agrees the claim is about the כתובה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be about a claim of no blood, so it does not prove anything about פתח פתוח, and שמואל's ruling is still needed.
